I want to build a rifle with my brother, we both know a fair bit about guns and their inner workings.

But we have made a rifle from individual parts, do you guys have suggestions for any resources we should start with? (I.E. where to shop, articles to read, dos n don't)

It's ideally going to be for precision/hunting, so ideally a larger caliber.

Also, we don't want to have to assemble every part, but at the same time, we don't want it to be as easy as snapping two receivers together.

Parts come down to cost. Your budget will get you higher quality components and lighter materials. An AR-15 can be built for as cheap as $400, and I have a few guns using a lot of lightweight titanium that are in the $3000-4000 in parts range.

Pretty much any caliber that fits in a AR-15 will meet whatever your definition of "precision hunting" is.

AR15 is going to be 223/556. If your looking for a larger caliber it would be an AR10 (308) or maybe a 300BLK.

AR's are very easy to build. I installed every little spring and pin out side of the bolt carrier so that's no biggie. Link a picture to a style AR you're thinking of

Brownells has a series of videos on how to build an AR with step by step instructions.

The InRange guys on full30.com are doing a series focusing on building an AR in line with Stoner's original intentions, but with modern materials and products.

The internet is full of opinions and thoughts, but it all boils down to what you're after. Which caliber, for starters? Shorter cartridges can fit in an AR-15 just fine, but longer ones would require any AR-10, and that will make things a bit more challenging.

Primary arms, brownells and palmetto state armory for parts. You can make it as simple or difficult as you want. Iraqveteran8888 has a good video on how to assemble to lower receiver. Personally I'd recommend an 80% lower receiver. It is easy if you follow directions, which people who have bad experiences with this route don't do. Morons like James Yeager go through three of them, give up and tell everyone else not to attempt it. I've made several of them with zero prior experience in metal work.

Might not be well received here but r/ar15 is a great resource.

Generally a standard ar in 556/223 isn't going to be suitable for deer but if you're willing to spend more you can look at other calibers on the same platform.

300 blackout is going to be almost identical to a standard build outside of the barrel. The ammo is more expensive so you'd probably want to look into reloading. Its really ideal for suppression because it works well with shorter barrels and since you're throwing a bigger piece of lead slower, you can shoot subsonic rounds. Both of those make it an ideal candidate for suppression.

There are other options but you need more and more specialized parts, more expensive ammo, etc. I'd recommend considering a standard 556 build and getting a separate hunting rifle. The cost will probably be around the same and is better to have two specialized tools than one one-size-fits-all option that isn't necessarily great at anything.

Most of the parts come together in kits. Lower, lower parts kit, buffer tube, buffer tube kit, trigger group, bolt carrier group, pistol grip, barrel, gas block. Then choose a barrel shroud, sights, muzzle device.

As others have already said, 223 is not legal for hunting big game, but It's fine for shooting coyotes or other pests. I would also recommend building it as a pistol first, so that you could switch to a shorter barrel blackout in the future. If you build it as a rifle, you can never convert it to a pistol. But a pistol can go back and forth. If you go .300 blk, you probably don't want a barrel much longer than 9".
